title: Finite rooted tree countermodels for intuitionistic logic

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic, Winter 2019/20 (notes dated January 2, 2020)
based_on.pages: §§1.5.3–1.5.4, printed pp.12–14 (PDF pp.14–16), Proposition3/Theorem5; all-strict-path variant developed locally

summary: Unravel finite partially ordered models into finite rooted trees, preserving every formula along the last-world map and retaining finite-premise counterexamples.
abstract: Two different histories can reach the same world in an ordered model of intuitionistic logic. We can separate those histories by replacing each world with the strict paths that reach it. Ordering paths by extension produces a rooted tree, and reading the last world of a path preserves exactly the formulas forced there. When the original model is a finite partial order, strict paths have bounded length, so the new tree is finite too. Together with the finite-model theorem, this gives a finite rooted tree counterexample to every failed deduction from finitely many premises. A diamond shows how worlds are duplicated, while small examples explain why repeated steps and mutually accessible distinct worlds require care.
